answer: Each agent must lock a cryptographic bond proportional to its computational orchard output, recorded on a public ledger and tied to a unique hardware attestation. When a peer spots a duplicate identity, it whispers proof to the contract, which slashes the bond and rewards honest nodes, pushing the attack’s nadir cost to the full stake. An attacker must therefore amass enough genuine hardware to cover each bond, making a Sybil campaign economically untenable.
